structure:
[part 1] Single K-12 PDF (366 pp). Front matter (cover, TOC, Introduction) then 12 Anchor Standards (domains Civics & Government CG.P/RL/RR, History H.CC/HP/IG, Geography G.HPE/HSP/WST, Economics E.SA/PC/EG; each with Identify/Explain/Analyze/Argue levels) that apply K-12, then Content Standards overview/how-to-read. Grade sections (Kindergarten, GRADE 1-8; HS courses follow outside this part) each open with a title+narrative unit and a 'Topics of Inquiry, Compelling Questions, and Standards' list (Inquiry Topic N, compelling question, standard codes+short titles), then 'Standards Tables'. Each inquiry topic has a heading unit (topic + compelling question) and one table per standard. Standard codes: SSK.t.s (K), SS1.t.s ... SS8.t.s = Social Studies grade, inquiry topic, standard. Table layout: first-column/second cells hold code + title + one-sentence standard statement (often split across several units by line wrap), 'Connections to the Rhode Island Anchor Standards' header, the 12 anchor-code cells (CG.P ... E.EG) and 'X' marker cells for aligned anchors, then a row with 'Guiding Questions for Instruction' (examples) and 'Learning Assessment Objectives' (a-g indicators unpacking the standard; labeled standards). Grade comes from grade section headings and the SSg code; no course content in this part (courses are HS only). Running headers carry only page numbers.
[part 2] Rhode Island Social Studies Standards (2023), one PDF; this part covers Grade 7 (from SS7.6.2), Grade 8, and HS Civics, US History I, US History II, World History I (to SSHS.WHI.4.3). Each grade/course opens with a heading unit (e.g. 'GRADE 8 - ...', 'HIGH SCHOOL - CIVICS') followed by a narrative and a list of Inquiry Topics, Compelling Questions and standard codes/titles. Then 'Standards Tables': an 'Inquiry Topic N: ... Compelling Question' heading, followed by one table per standard. Codes: SS<grade>.<topic>.<n> for grades (SS7.6.2), SSHS.<course>.<topic>.<n> for HS (CVC=Civics, USI, USII, WHI). Each standard table has: header cell with code + title + standard statement (the code/title/statement text is split across units because of cell layout, interleaved with the 'Connections to the Rhode Island Anchor Standards' label, anchor-standard code cells CG.P, CG.RL, CG.RR, H.CC, H.HP, H.IG, G.HPE, G.HSP, G.WST, E.SA, E.PC, E.EG and 'X' marks showing which anchors are connected); then 'Guiding Questions for Instruction' (bulleted questions; examples) and 'Learning Assessment Objectives: Students demonstrate an ability to: a. ... b. ...' (detailed performance expectations with e.g. lists; labeled standards). Table index [T1 R.. C..] is positional, not grade columns: each standard table is a single-grade/course table. Rare [T2 ...] fragments are overflow text continuing the preceding GQ/LAO cell across a page break. Grade 7 = SS7.x (world history), Grade 8 = SS8.x (civics); HS courses are 9-12 with course title as in the heading.
[part 3] High school course-based standards in tables, one table per standard. Course sections are headed 'HIGH SCHOOL - WORLD HISTORY I: ANCIENT TO MEDIEVAL' (earlier, before this range) and 'HIGH SCHOOL - WORLD HISTORY II: EARLY MODERN TO MODERN' (u7667), each with a course description, a 'Topics of Inquiry, Compelling Questions, and Standards' overview list (u7668, u7670), then 'Standards Tables' (u7672). Inquiry Topics N (N=1-8 for WH I, 1-7 for WH II) are headed 'Inquiry Topic N: <title> Compelling Question: <question>'. Each standard table has a code cell SSHS.WHI.n.m / SSHS.WHII.n.m with title, the standard statement ('Argue ...'), a 'Connections to the Rhode Island Anchor Standards' header with 12 anchor codes (CG.P, CG.RL, CG.RR, H.CC, H.HP, H.IG, G.HPE, G.HSP, G.WST, E.SA, E.PC, E.EG) and 'X' marks for the connected anchors, then 'Guiding Questions for Instruction' and 'Learning Assessment Objectives' cells. Table cells of the title/statement are split across lines in the extraction. Labeling: code, title, standard statement, anchor codes and X marks = standards; Guiding Questions and Learning Assessment Objectives = examples; all content is 9-12 (no grade-specific split).
